title: Reliability Testing for Natural Language Processing Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model robustness through dimension-specific worst-case tests using adversarial perturbations of orthography, morphology, lexicon, syntax, and dialectal variations (e.g., African American English, code-mixing).
Applying constrained adversarial attacks as reliability tests by perturbing inputs with different gender pronouns, names, and genderlects to observe performance degradation.
Testing worst-case model performance by perturbing text with names, reclaimed slurs, and race-aligned language varieties.
Conducting reliability testing by sampling perturbations that reflect age and generation-aligned language styles.
Evaluating system reliability when encountering input variations containing names and reclaimed slurs associated with specific religions.
Using adversarial and average-case test sets that include reclaimed slurs and terminology related to sexual orientation to measure model performance.
Testing model reliability against inputs containing specific associated adjectives related to disability status.
Measuring changes in system performance when perturbing text with varying location names (cities, countries) and regional figures of speech.
Using geographic locations as proxies for socioeconomic status during targeted reliability testing and observing differential system impact.
